Anti-Eyesore Engineering

(wit the homies) · ACCESSIBLE SECTION 215 EVIDENCE PACK
Site: 317–319 Lower High St, Watford WD17 2JD Civic Tenure: 1832–1959 (127 Years as King William IV) Documented: Dec 2023 – Nov 2026 Goal: Section 215 Notice + Makerspace & Biodiversity Net Gain Alternative

127 years of public life (1832–1959) — now a stalled eyesore. Let's turn it into a community makerspace & green corridor.

Right beside the Bushey Arches railway viaduct sits 317–319 Lower High Street. First recorded in 1832 as a beer house that predated the viaduct and served the workers who built it, the King William IV ("King Billy") stood as a neighbourhood gathering place for nearly 130 years until 1959.

Today, it sits unsecured and deteriorating on a daily bus and walking route between Watford, Bushey, and Oxhey. Throughout Jan–Nov 2026, cheap new windows and doors were mortared in and then left to stall—leaving jagged glass at street level, a ripped-off drainpipe, and pooling water indoors for eleven months—even as a paper conversion into 8 one-bedroom flats (26/00641/CTR, approved 9 Oct 2026, alongside 26/00402/FUL) moved through the portal.

This page is an accessible, anonymous Section 215 Evidence Pack for local partners, makerspace organisers, environmental groups, and Watford Borough Council. We are calling for a Section 215 Notice to make the building safe—paired with a ready-to-deploy, insured meanwhile-use makerspace & Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG) plan.

THE RALLYING CALL // WATFORD OBSERVER (8 DEC 2017) → NOV 2026

Nine Years of “Looking at the Future Use”

In December 2017, the Watford Observer ran the headline: “‘Eyesore’ Chalk Hill car park at Bushey Arches is dumping ground for cars.” The council stated it was “looking at the future use of this area to ensure it adds value to the locality and community.” A local reader translated that instantly: “How many flats would fit on here?”

Almost a decade later, the Heras fences are still up, adjacent Chalk Hill plots have been marketed for £7 million, and active local organisers—musicians, instrument repairers (Good Vibrations Watford), cyclists, and makers—are told there are no premises available. This is the same town whose high street anchored UK Grime in its public settings (Sidewinder 2002 at Ocean; Eskimo Dance 2002–2005 at Area). We don’t need another seven years of neglect or another speculative block with zero community space. Wrap the eyesore in a cared-for, experimental zone—and open the doors to the people already building here.

Section 215 Evidence Pack: Documented Deterioration (2025 → 2026)

01 // BEFORE & AFTER RECORD
What is a Section 215 Notice in plain English? Under Section 215 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Watford Borough Council can serve a legal notice requiring a property owner to clean up, secure, and repair a building whose condition harms the look and safety of the neighbourhood. Because we have dated photographs from late 2025 and across 2026, we can prove this site isn't just quietly empty—it is actively worsening due to abandoned works.
Before // Site Visits: November – December 2025
  • Original black commercial double doors and roller shutters were still in place (only one lower glass pane cracked).
  • Rainwater guttering and black downpipes along the "ONE WAY" yard wall were intact and draining.
  • The building was vacant and overgrown, but still largely weatherproofed against rain ingress.
After // Stalled Works: January – November 2026 (11 Months)
  • Original doors were ripped out and cheap white uPVC windows/French doors were mortared in—then left unsecured and smashed through.
  • The rainwater downpipe along the "ONE WAY" wall was torn off and left lying on the ground.
  • Water now pools across the ground floor with spreading ceiling damp, directly behind the main bus-route shopfront.
Regional Context — The Adjacent Mega Empty Site (Oct 2025 → May 2026): Immediately next to 317 Lower High Street sits a massive adjoining empty site along the viaduct. In October 2025, concrete jersey barriers blocked the edge. In May 2026, the adjacent site was cleared, boarded up, shuttered out, and sealed behind heavy metal anti-climb gates. While out of initial licensing scope, both plots form one linked Bushey Arches dead zone. Open Site B Dossier (April 2026 Arson, 3D LiDAR & Pyrophilous Fungi) →

Why This Works for Everyone (Enforcement + Makerspace + Biodiversity Net Gain)

02 // VALUE PROPOSITION

For Local Creatives & Makers

Watford and Bushey don't lack talent—they lack affordable, street-level places to build, rehearse, repair, and gather without paying £100/month memberships.

  • Modular & Demountable: Everything we install (workbenches, acoustic panels, living walls) is built to pack down cleanly if long-term works ever resume.
  • Hands-On Skill Sharing: Woodworking, ceramics, bike/electronics repair, sound composition, and community health drop-ins under one roof.

For the Owner & Council

Borrowing from the Dutch anti-kraak (meanwhile-use) model, we offer a low-risk, insured custodian arrangement that solves an active headache.

  • Stops Asset Decay: Immediate make-safe glazing, cleared glass, restored downpipes, and daytime occupation to deter vandalism.
  • Zero Block to Sale: Flexible 28-day rolling break clause and potential Empty Property Business Rates relief via a local charitable/trust wrapper.

Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG)

Today, this corner is sealed concrete, anti-climb gates, broken glass, and ruptured drainage. Our alternative turns it into a living urban stepping stone aligned with Environment Act 2021 Biodiversity Net Gain goals.

  • Green Corridor Link: Connects Oxhey Park Extension with the mature sycamore belt bordering Bushey Arches.
  • Flood Attenuation: Reconnecting the ripped-off downpipes into modular rain-gardens slows stormwater runoff at a known local flood pinch-point.

Built on Real Local Craft: Makerspace & Ecological Testbed

03 // WHAT WE BUILD INSIDE

This isn't a generic "pop-up" pitch—it is an initiative of gathering rooted in place-based action-research. Formulated for the roadside-adjacent Bushey Arches corridor in January 2025 (Architecturing Necessary Possibles) following local observation and pivotal questions, this avenue has been shaped through ongoing local conversation, ecological study, and precedent research (including Makespace Oxford, Material Cultures, LJ Works, Urban Reef, and TAC Eindhoven). Rather than prescribing a fixed product, it treats architecturing as a verb in the social domain—inviting neighbours into agentic, material social engagement and a library economy of collective solidarity where asking questions and sharing skills weaves the local fabric.

#living-infrastructure

Agentic material and ecological prototyping—brownfield restoration, native pollinator beds, natural-material acoustics, and a street-facing plant exchange.

#makers-and-craft

An open initiative of gathering and shared workbench—supporting modular self-build, vernacular craft, everyday repair, and weekend skill-sharing.

#study-and-care

Free community blood-pressure/health drop-ins, Warm Hub access, homework club, and a neighbourhood research library.

#sound-and-culture

Local record exchange, composition club, and low-cost rehearsal space insulated with locally grown biomaterials.

Statutory, Planning, Ecological & Archival References

  • Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Section 215: Statutory power for local planning authorities to require proper maintenance of land/buildings adversely affecting neighbourhood amenity.
  • Environment Act 2021 (Part 6 & Schedule 14): Mandatory Biodiversity Net Gain (10%+) framework and urban green corridor recovery principles.
  • Localism Act 2011 (Part 5, Chapter 3): Assets of Community Value (ACV) and the Community Right to Bid.
